newsitem.title: UK: IBCA cuts UBS individual rating to A/B.
newsitem.headline: IBCA cuts UBS individual rating to A/B.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Tuesday it had downgraded its individual rating of Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) from A to A/B.
But it said it had maintained the bank's ratings of short-term A1 plus, long-term AAA and legal 1.
UBS is one of the few abnks left in the world with AAA ratings from the major credit rating agencies. On Monday, Standard and Poor's put the bank on its CreditWatch list.
IBCA said that its rating action followed the announcement that UBS intends to take a three billion Swiss franc special loan loss provision against its 1996 profits.

"The provision is for expected future risk on its domestic loan portfolio over the next two to three years. The special loan loss provisio, will be provided in addition to the normal loan loss provision of about 1.4 bln Swiss francs in 1996," IBCA said.
"As a result UBS will report a post-tax loss of about 0.5 bln Swiss francs for 1996."

IBCA added that in its opinion, in deciding to create this specific provision for future losses, UBS was acknowledging not only the poor conditions now prevailing in the Swiss economy as a whole but also a deterioration in its own asset quality.
"It is for this reason that IBCA has decided to lower UBS's Individual rating to A/B from A," it said.
